review: Reviewed Wren's round-256 request (hand-join-fiber-cords: learn and perform a bare-hand end-to-end joining knot on two owned finished fiber cords, with inspection, bounded two-end load trials, untying and cancellation; dry safe footing and free space; Wren holds one straight two-ply reed cord with a 0.34 m centreline, previously tied and untied, and a second cord; actual lengths, widths, condition and gripping tails must decide feasibility; inputs two exact owned cord ids, a personally learned method and an optional bounded force and duration, with no tools, anchors or added fiber; costs to be determined and disclosed, paid progress preserved and cancellation defined; both cords and their lengths conserved, measured geometry and failures reported, inspection establishing no strength, only a real bounded trial reporting holding, slipping or damage, and later untying where physically possible) and the World Agent's develop review (learning 3): a general hand-join-fiber-cords with modes attempt, inspect, trial, untie and cancel, two distinct exact cord ids, method sheet-bend, workId for resumption, a join id for later operations, trialForce above 0 to 10 N and trialDuration above 0 to 60 s; study 3 rounds at 0.2 energy; attempt at most 4 worked rounds at 0.5 (measure and select bight and crossing, pass the second end, wrap and tuck, dress and release-check); inspection 1 round at 0.2; trial 1 round at 0.5; untie at most 2 rounds at 0.5; cancel immediate and free; 0.0005 wear per worked round on each manipulated cord, once, and no material fee; a single sheet bend with the bight chosen from measured suitability, finite-width paths and crossings, material bend limits, a 0.02 m clear opening and a retained 0.02 m pinch for each passage, short tails of at least 0.02 m plus the local width and 0.05 m trial grips kept 0.01 m clear of the bend; a centreline ledger per cord; the join as a relation of both conserved items; a versioned joining law with finite-width geometry and a material-dependent slip and retention response, implementing a minimal documented friction mechanism where none exists; trial force bounded by the request, 200 N x health/100, the 10000 N/m grip limit of each gripped width, span and actual failure, recording requested and achieved force, duration, grip slip, tail displacement, geometry, condition, extension, strand damage and failure location; rupture into reconciled owned fragments; atomic reservation of both items, pause, resume by workId, cancel and death rules; untying that reverses passes and may jam; reusable visual metadata and labelled events; no reward. The specification is self-consistent and every gated physical transition can be given an explicit declared rule, so this is a simplified real mechanism, not a first release. Implemented hand-join-fiber-cords@1 in scope long-ex16 (new module packages/world-core/src/long-fiber-cord-join.ts, export LONG_FIBER_CORD_JOIN, handler long.hand-join-fiber-cords, events prefixed cord-join-, law cord-bend@1), registered at the end of V7_PACKAGES with package dependencies foundation-open@1, hand-twist-fiber-cord@1 and hand-tie-cord-knot@1; learning 3 with learningEnergy 0.2, so each study round is paid; no prerequisite, and neither cord ability is required; the ability serializes to 3,486 code units within the 3,500 limit; references are empty, so cordIds and joinId accept exact ids only. Modes and costs: attempt (cordIds, method sheet-bend) reserves both cords atomically and pays four rounds of 0.5 energy (measure-form-bight, pass-second-end, wrap-and-tuck, dress-release-check), continuing on each worked round and resumable only by workId; a loose wrapped-and-tucked bend left by cancellation needs only the dressing round; inspect (joinId or workId) costs 0.2, changes nothing and records an unverified finding; trial (joinId, trialForce, trialDuration) costs 0.5; untie (joinId) pays two rounds of 0.5 (withdraw-tucked-end, withdraw-through-bight); cancel is free. Every validation (mastery, per-mode arguments, two distinct exact ids of own finished cords or fragments, no active knot, join or reservation, strand and friction law, two-ply section, condition 0.5, the material-independent minimum geometry, dry footing and the work circle, energy, no unfinished own work) precedes any charge, so refusals spend nothing; no material is consumed. Modeling assumptions of cord-bend@1: the width w of each cord is the fiber-cord@1 grip width (two ply diameters) and its centreline is its overall length; a = (w of bight + w of other)/2 is the centre distance of two touching cords; the tightest radius each cord takes without cracking is the cord-knot@1 bend limit measured on the live item (w x 0.5/(index - 0.5), 2.5 widths for reed), reported only as radii; crown radius rB = max(bight limit, a), opened at formation so its inner gap clears max(0.02 m, other width); bight path = pi rB + 4 x other width (two legs, each crossed by one passage and one wrap width); the other cord passes up through the bight (one bight width), once round both legs whose centres lie 2 rB apart at radius rW = max(its limit, a), its arcs touching the outer sides of the legs (path 2 max(0, 2 rB - 2(rW - a)) + 2 pi rW), and under its own entering part (one own width); the method gives each short tail exactly 0.02 m + its width and the rest to the standing part, and a standing part below the 0.02 m standing pinch is a measured shortfall; dressing seats both arcs at their limits and shares any formation slack equally between tail and standing part; the bight is the assignment that fits and leaves both standing parts a trial grip, else the one with the longer shorter standing part, then the wider and then the better-conditioned cord as bight, then input order, and both candidates are recorded; the pre-cost check ignores the material limit (the least any fiber could need), so only the paid first round can find a bend-limit shortfall. Retention is a new minimal friction law: static fiber-on-fiber friction mu = 0.3 for reed on reed (dry plant-fiber cordage lies near 0.25-0.5; wetness, wear and dynamic friction are not represented; any other fiber is an explicit unsupported-material refusal); contact angles pi x a/rB for the bight tail (the crown round the passing cord) and 2 pi x a/rW for the other tail (one turn round both legs), an arc wider than what it wraps touching over the share a/radius of its angle; each tail is nipped on two faces by its crossing (holding factor 2 mu); a tail is self-locking when 2 mu e^(mu x angle) >= 1 and otherwise holds the 5 N dressing pull of the fiber-cord@1 sample test amplified to 2 mu x 5 N/(e^(-mu x angle) - 2 mu); the release check fails if that slip load does not exceed 5 N or a tail is short. For Wren's two equal 8.1 mm reed cords this gives contact angles 1.26 and 2.51 rad, a self-locking wrap and a bight-tail slip load near 35 N, so trials up to 10 N hold and slipping is reachable only with a looser seated bend. Trial: each hand grips 0.05 m of a different standing part kept 0.01 m clear; force = min(trialForce, 200 N x health/100, 10000 N/m x the narrower width, slip load, breaking force); each cord's breaking force in the bend is the fiber-cord@1 breaking force divided by 1 + w/(2 x its loaded arc radius), the cord-knot@1 curvature rule, applicable because it depends only on a tensioned cord's width and bend radius and not on the overhand topology; extension and creep use the fiber-cord@1 stiffness and creep over each cord's loaded span (standing part beyond the grip plus its path), retained creep lengthening that standing part with volume kept; load above half a cord's breaking force breaks that share of its strands; outcomes are held, grip-lost, slipped (a tail is drawn through and both cords come apart, its displacement recorded) or broke (the weaker cord parts at its crown or at the entry of its turn into two owned fragments whose lengths sum to its centreline at the recorded break point, with 0.1-unit quantities in proportion to length and at least 0.1 each and condition halved, while the other cord is freed straight); a seated bend takes up no further slack below its slip load. Untying needs condition 0.5 in both cords and a 0.02 m pinch on the end; an arc that hugs what it wraps (conformity 1) and carried more than half its breaking force jams. The retained states (wrapped, tied) give both cords the role joined and reserve them for the join id, so knots, straight trials, transfers and other joins are refused; the unretained bight and threaded states open on any release with a cord-join-released event; death stops open work, leaves both cords where the person died and keeps a retained bend bound. Wear: the 0.0005 per worked round is the existing fiber-cord@1 per-round wear applied once per item per round, by hand-twist-fiber-cord@1 for cords and fragments and by this package for joined cords, which no other environment wears. Events cord-join-started, -stage, -infeasible, -paused, -resumed, -released, -tied, -slipped, -resisted, -untied, -cancelled, -stopped, -inspected, -trial, -damaged and -broken carry reusable view metadata (component cord-join reusing fiber-cord: join, work and both item ids, method and law, each cord's part, color, width, standing part, path, tail, schematic centreline and condition, the over/under crossing list, radii and a status of incomplete, geometrically-infeasible, tied-but-untested, held-at-recorded-load, slipped, jammed, broken, released or untied, with a completed appearance only for a dressed, release-checked bend); visualComponents is empty. Bounded verified findings use the existing personal records keyed by materials, widths and outcome; the tied event carries no qualified flag, so no milestone, pleasure, satisfaction or comfort follows. Reuse: hand-twist-fiber-cord@1 (law fiber-cord@1) through its existing FIBER_CORD export, and hand-tie-cord-knot@1 (revision hand-tie-cord-knot@1, handler long.hand-tie-cord-knot, law cord-knot@1) through a new append-only CORD_KNOT export of its bend measurement, knot state and hand constants; both abilities keep their text and behavior, and the overhand topology, path formula and non-spilling assertion are not reused. Tests in apps/simulator/test/long-ex16-hand-join-fiber-cords.test.ts cover scope, learning, size and wording, the four paid rounds on two cords of Wren's actual size with closed ledgers and conserved stock, a paid measured shortfall and pre-cost refusals, the assignment and a tie without trial grips, held, hand-limited, damaging, breaking and slipping trials, untying with damage and jam resistance, pause, resume, cancel and loose-bend dressing, inspection, wear, owner-only rules and death; a local check on the paused round-256 checkpoint also showed Wren's item-250-wren-2847 forming the bight for item-226-wren-2532 and the dressed bend holding 10 N for 60 s.
